items.rootCause: apps/mobile/src/net/connectivity.ts useConnectivityWatch checked GET /health once when Home mounted, and checked again in the background only while the status was already 'offline'. Home's focus effect also checked once each time Home came back into view. The app has no network-state module (no NetInfo or expo-network, and nothing can be installed now). So when flight mode went on while Home stayed open and in view, no check ever ran. The status stayed 'online', the banner never showed, and the ranked 'עוד סיבוב' stayed active.
items.fix: connectivity.ts: new CONNECTIVITY.onlineRecheckMs = 10000 and new watchConnectionWhileShown(). While the status is not 'offline' and the app is in the foreground (AppState not 'background' or 'inactive'), it calls the shared check() every 10 s. It also checks at once when AppState comes back to 'active'. Its return value stops both. While offline it does nothing, because the existing 5 s recheck already runs then; the back-online path (and appProgress's offline->online sync) is unchanged. HomeScreen.tsx: useFocusEffect(watchConnectionWhileShown). So the polling runs only while Home is the screen shown. It stops under a game, the search or any other screen, and in the background. Banner, dimmed 'עוד סיבוב' and '· דורש חיבור' are the existing UI, unchanged (no new strings).
items.test: apps/mobile/src/screens/home/__tests__/OfflineBeforeGame.test.tsx: (1) 'QA account-home-offline: flight mode on while Home stays open brings the banner within seconds'. Home opens online with a ranked last play. The health check then goes false, and timers advance by onlineRecheckMs with no focus change. Expected: banner 'אין חיבור לאינטרנט. משחקים מדורגים לא זמינים', play-again disabled with 'מדורג · 2 שחקנים · מהיר · דורש חיבור', and a tap stays on '/'. Back online, after recheckMs the banner is gone and 'דורש חיבור' is gone. I confirmed this test fails with the focus hook removed. (2) 'no online checks while another screen is over Home': History is pushed over Home, timers advance 30 s, and the check count stays the same. apps/mobile/src/net/__tests__/connectivity.test.ts covers three things. The CONNECTIVITY constants now include onlineRecheckMs 10000. While online, the watch checks every 10 s and sees the connection go, then stays quiet once offline. It makes no checks in the background, checks once on 'active', and makes none after stop. All 46 related suites pass (home, net, ranked e2e, a11yAudit, appProgress, startupGraph). tsc, eslint and prettier are clean, with LF line endings.
items.deviceCheck: Phone connected by USB, online, signed in to a verified email/password test account. 1) Home > שחק > מדורג > 2 שחקנים > מהיר > מצא יריב, then ביטול חיפוש, then Back until Home shows. 2) Check that Home shows 'עוד סיבוב' with 'מדורג · 2 שחקנים · מהיר' under it. 3) Keep Home open and turn flight mode on (adb shell cmd connectivity airplane-mode enable). Touch nothing and wait about 15 s at most (one 10 s check, and on some phones up to 5 s more before the request fails). Expected: under the card, a banner with a crossed-out Wi-Fi icon, 'אין חיבור לאינטרנט' with 'משחקים מדורגים לא זמינים' under it ('בודק…' may flash during a check). 'עוד סיבוב' is dimmed and its subtitle ends with '· דורש חיבור'. 4) Tap 'עוד סיבוב': nothing happens, no search screen. 5) Turn flight mode off (adb shell cmd connectivity airplane-mode disable) and wait a few seconds on Home: the banner goes, and 'עוד סיבוב' is active again without 'דורש חיבור'. 6) Extra check: with flight mode on, send the app to the background and bring it back. The banner should show at once (a check runs on return to the foreground).

rep.notes: There is no native network-state module in apps/mobile (no @react-native-community/netinfo or expo-network), and npm install is not allowed now. The fix therefore uses the existing GET /health check on a 10 s timer, limited to while Home is shown and the app is in the foreground. While offline, the existing 5 s recheck takes over unchanged. If a NetInfo module is added later, watchConnectionWhileShown is the one place to switch to an event listener. The report says that after 'חזרה לבית' from the search error no banner appeared either. That route (dismissTo('/')) already ran a check from Home's focus effect, so the banner should have come within the 5 s check timeout. Now the 10 s watch also covers it. If it still fails on the phone after this fix, it is worth watching how long the health request takes to fail in flight mode on that phone. There are no string changes, so no i18n check was needed. The server was not touched.

issues.problem: After going offline, the banner can take up to about 15 s to appear (10 s interval plus up to 5 s for the health timeout), and 5 s to 10 s is the usual case. The catalog's step 4 only says to wait a few seconds in Home ('מחכים כמה שניות בבית'), so a tester who waits about 5 s can see a false fail.
issues.evidence: connectivity.ts: onlineRecheckMs 10000 and timeoutMs 5000. In flight mode on Android, OkHttp usually fails at once (DNS or ENETUNREACH), so the usual delay is 0 to 10 s. The fixer's deviceCheck already says to wait about 15 s.
issues.suggestion: When the result is checked on the phone, wait about 15 s, or change the catalog's step 4 to say so. A shorter interval (for example 5 s) is optional and costs about 2x more GETs while Home is open.

issues.problem: Home now re-renders about twice every 10 s while it is shown and online. useConnectivityWatch subscribes to the whole store, and each periodic check toggles 'checking' on and off. Nothing visible changes, because 'בודק…' only shows inside the offline banner.
issues.evidence: HomeScreen.tsx:95 const connectivity = useConnectivityWatch() returns the full state from useConnectivity(), and check() runs set({checking:true}) and then set({... checking:false}).
issues.suggestion: Optional: let Home read only status, plus 'checking' only while offline, through a selector. This is not needed to fix the bug.

issues.problem: On a slow but working mobile network, a single /health call that takes longer than 5 s now marks the app offline. Because Home now checks every 10 s, this happens far more often than before. The banner then shows briefly, TalkBack reads 'אין חיבור לאינטרנט', and it clears on the next 5 s check.
issues.evidence: watchConnectionWhileShown calls check() every 10 s while online. check() turns status to 'offline' after one failed attempt, and the Home Announcer reads the line whenever offline is true.
issues.suggestion: Optional: when a periodic check fails while online, mark the app offline only after 2 failures in a row. The QA item does not need this.

issues.problem: This is outside this item's scope. ModesScreen and GameTypeScreen (ranked) use useConnectivityWatch without this periodic check, so going offline while one of them stays open is still missed. That is the same blind spot this fix closes for Home.
issues.evidence: grep: ModesScreen.tsx:94 and GameTypeScreen.tsx:68 use useConnectivityWatch() only. watchConnectionWhileShown is used only in HomeScreen.tsx:138.
issues.suggestion: If QA reports the same thing for the Modes screen, add useFocusEffect(watchConnectionWhileShown) there too.

items.rootCause: The result's 'למפה' (and Android back on the result) called router.dismissTo('/levels') with no params. The map stays mounted under the stage route the whole time, so it kept its own React state. That state is the choice picked earlier (L001 or L008) and the scroll position. LevelMapScreen moved the choice and the scroll only when currentLevel changed (seenCurrent and follow(current)). Replaying an older stage never changes the current stage, so the map came back on the old pick. A second problem: the map read the 'select' param only in its initial useState. Even 'לשלב הבא' with the quick entry off (which already passed select) could not move a map that was already mounted.
items.fix: apps/mobile/app/levels/play.tsx: the result's 'למפה' and back-on-result now go through resultToMap. It calls dismissTo({pathname:'/levels', params:{select, pick}}). select is the stage after the one just played, the same one 'לשלב הבא' would start (nextAfterAttempt, moved into a shared nextOf). If no next stage is open (a gate still shut, or the last stage), select is the played stage. pick = `${routeKey}:${run.n}` changes on every run, so the same stage can be chosen twice in a row. A leave with no result (onLeave, back before the stage started) still goes to the plain map, as before. The quick-entry-off 'לשלב הבא' uses the same toMapAt. apps/mobile/app/levels/index.tsx reads 'pick' and passes it on. apps/mobile/src/screens/levels/LevelMapScreen.tsx: a new select/pick pair (chosenTag) sets the choice during render, after the current-stage logic so it wins. An effect then scrolls the map to that stage at 40% of the height (animated, not under Reduced Motion). A 'held' ref keeps the map on the chosen stage when levels.db is read again a moment later and moves the current stage on. Any tap on a node or gate, a drag, or a chapter jump lets go of it, and the old behaviour returns. The first-open select and the loop-15 recreate restore (the select param kept by flowStack restoredHomeState, and levels/shownResult.ts) work as before. After a recreate, the map now comes back on the chosen stage instead of '-'. No new strings, so no i18n change.
items.test: New: LevelMapScreen.test.tsx 'QA levels-to-map: a stage chosen from outside again…' (unit). The map is open with stage 6 current. Tap node 1, then a new select L002 arrives: the panel shows 'שלב 2' and the map scrolls to openOffset(2). A later current change (records played(6)) does not scroll away. The same select with a new pick chooses it again. After the player taps a node, a moving current stage scrolls the map again. New: 'the way through, he/en › QA levels-to-map: an old stage replayed…' runs through the real routes (renderApp with a Stack _layout, so the map stays mounted as on the phone, the real LevelsRoute and the real LevelPlayFlow). Play L001, then twice: tap node 1, 'שחק', 'מוכן?', finish, 'למפה'. Each time the same mounted map shows the panel on 'שלב 2', scrolls to openOffset(2), and the URL is /levels?select=L002&pick=…. Updated: levelPlayBack.test.tsx (back on the result now dismisses to {pathname:'/levels', params:{select: next stage, pick}}). Updated: recreatedFlowStack.test.tsx ('למפה' then shows MAP L00(n+1), and a recreate after it keeps that map). With the baseline sources put back, 6 of these tests fail; with the fix all pass. Ran screens/levels, recreatedFlowStack, levels.e2e, a11yAudit and ModesAndGameType: 31 suites, 794 tests pass. tsc -p apps/mobile is clean, eslint on the changed files is clean, prettier was applied, and every changed file is LF.
items.deviceCheck:
Needs a new APK with this change. On Phone 1, signed in with stages already played (L001–L017 or more):
A) Home → 'משחק חדש' → 'אימון בשלבים'. On the map, tap L001 (a played stage) and press 'שחק'. Play it, then on the result press 'לשלב הבא' several times until L007's result. Press 'למפה'. Expect: the map scrolls to L008, the bottom panel reads 'שלב 8 · …', and L007 shows the stars it got. It must not be the top of chapter 1 or 'שלב 1'.
B) Tap L008 on the map and press 'שחק'. Use 'לשלב הבא' to reach L010 (boss) and finish it. Press 'למפה'. Expect: the map on L011 with the panel 'שלב 11 · …'. If the chapter 2 gate is still shut (L011 locked): the map on L010 with the panel 'שלב 10'.
C) Same stage twice in a row: tap L001, play it, 'למפה' → the panel is on 'שלב 2'. Tap L001 again, play it again, 'למפה' → the panel is again on 'שלב 2' (not 'שלב 1').
D) Android back on a result (instead of 'למפה') does the same as A–C.
E) Play the current stage (from 'המשך · שלב N'), then 'למפה': the map is on stage N+1, with the gold road and token moving on as before and the stars on N.
F) Back from 'מוכן?' (before the stage starts) still returns to the map on the stage that was chosen, with nothing moved.
G) After C, change the display size (wm density) or the font size: the map comes back on the same chosen stage.

rep.notes: Choice made: 'the stage after the one just played' means the stage the result's 'לשלב הבא' would start (played+1 when it is open), which matches the QA examples (L007→L008, L010→L011). One case changes. In the earlier 'working' report, L018 was played while L019–L033 had already been played, and 'למפה' went to the current stage L034. Now it opens on L019, the stage after the one played. The map's token, the gold road and the 'השלב הבא' ring still mark L034. If Moshe prefers 'the new current stage when progress moved', only resultToMap in play.tsx needs to change. The expo-router test helper's default navigator is a Slot, which remounts the map, so the old bug did not show there. The new route test therefore gives renderApp a Stack _layout, as in the real app. To prove the new tests fail, I briefly copied the three baseline sources (git show refs/qa/snap-loop17) over my files and then copied my versions back from the scratchpad. All three had no diff from the snapshot apart from mine. No adb, build, deploy or npm install. No git state commands.

issues.problem: The fix changes a case that QA had already passed. When the player plays the current stage and later stages are already played, 'למפה' no longer opens on the new current stage (the 'השלב הבא' ring). It now opens on played+1. In the QA report's own 'working' example (L018 played, L019–L033 already played), the map used to open on L034 with 'השלב הבא'. It will now open with the panel on 'שלב 19', while the token, the gold road and the 'השלב הבא' ring stay on L034, which may be off screen. On the re-test, the tester may mark this as a fail, since they accepted L034 as correct.
issues.evidence: In apps/mobile/app/levels/play.tsx, resultToMap = onMap(nextOf(played) ?? level.id). nextOf is nextAfterAttempt, which returns nextLevelId(levelId, ...), meaning played+1 when it is open. In LevelMapScreen.tsx, the new chosenTag render block sets selected to preselected after the seenCurrent block, so it wins. 'held' then keeps the scroll on it: useEffect(() => follow(held.current ?? current), [current]). The fixer's own notes admit the L018 to L019 change. The QA task text says the current-stage case works: 'למפה' opened on L034 with the tag 'השלב הבא'.
issues.suggestion: Choose explicitly, and keep both QA examples green. In resultToMap: if the played stage was the current one before the attempt, and the attempt moved the current stage, select currentLevel(withAttempt(records, level.id, played.outcome), openedNow). Otherwise keep nextOf(played) ?? level.id. This gives L018 to L034 and normal play N to N+1, and replaying L007 still gives L008. Or have Moshe confirm the L019 reading before the APK. Add a test for each choice.

issues.problem: The 'held' ref is not released when the map comes back without a chosen stage. In that case chosenTag goes to null (plain dismissTo('/levels') from onLeave, a fallback's 'לבית', or back on 'מוכן?'). held keeps the old stage, so if the current stage changes later while no stage is chosen (a levels.db refresh, or progress synced after sign-in while the map is shown), the map scrolls to that old stage and not to the current one. The panel follows current, because the seenCurrent block still moves 'selected', so the panel and the scroll can disagree. This is rare, and it is a regression from the baseline, where follow(current) always ran.
issues.evidence: In LevelMapScreen.tsx, held is set only in followChosen (if preselected === null it returns early without clearing). It is cleared only in onNode, onGate, onJump and onDrag. The current-stage effect is useEffect(() => follow(held.current ?? current), [current]). In play.tsx, onLeave={() => onMap()} and the back before the stage starts both call leave(), which is router.dismissTo('/levels') with no params. The POP_TO in expo-router's StackRouter then replaces the params, so select and pick become undefined.
issues.suggestion: In the chosenTag !== seenChosen block, or in followChosen, set held.current = null when preselected is null. A plain return to the map then lets the current stage lead again.

issues.problem: No test covers the exact QA path: a stage picked on the map, then several 'לשלב הבא' (quick entry, the same route with run.n going up), then 'למפה'. The route test only does: pick node 1, play, 'למפה'. The logic should work, because level and run.n come from the current run, but the reported path itself is not covered.
issues.evidence: The new route test in LevelMapScreen.test.tsx ('the way through' › QA levels-to-map) calls playOnce, which presses level-panel-play, finish and level-result-map. It never presses level-result-next.
issues.suggestion: Extend the route test: tap node 1, play, press 'לשלב הבא' twice (L002, then L003), then 'למפה'. Expect the panel on stage 4 and select=L004 in the URL.

items.rootCause: The result's 'למפה' (and Android back on the result) called router.dismissTo('/levels') with no params. The map stays mounted under the stage route, so it kept its own React state: the stage picked earlier (L001 or L008) and the scroll position. LevelMapScreen moved the choice and the scroll only when currentLevel changed (seenCurrent and follow(current)). Replaying an older stage never changes the current stage, so the map came back on the old pick. The 'select' param was also read only in the first useState, so even the quick-entry-off 'לשלב הבא', which already passed select, could not move a map that was already mounted.
items.fix:
apps/mobile/app/levels/play.tsx: the result's 'למפה' and back on the result go through resultToMap. It calls dismissTo({pathname:'/levels', params:{select, pick}}). pick = routeKey:run.n changes on every run, so the same stage can be chosen twice in a row. select comes from a new pure function, mapAfterAttempt (in mapModel.ts):
(a) A stage played for the first time that moved the current stage on: select is the new current stage. This keeps the case QA already passed (review issue 1): L018 played with L019-L033 played before goes to L034, 'השלב הבא'. In plain play, N goes to N+1.
(b) A stage played before (a replay): select is the stage after it, the one 'לשלב הבא' starts (L007 to L008, L010 to L011).
(c) No next stage open (a gate still shut, or L300): select is the played stage.
'First play' is read once when the run starts, from levels.db's records before the attempt (plays === 0). For a result restored after a recreate, the records already include the attempt, so the check there is plays <= 1. If levels.db is not read yet or there is no account, it counts as false and rule (b) applies.
A leave with no result (onLeave, back on 'מוכן?') still goes to the plain map. The quick-entry-off 'לשלב הבא' uses the same toMapAt. apps/mobile/app/levels/index.tsx passes 'pick' on.
LevelMapScreen.tsx: a select/pick pair (chosenTag) sets the choice during render, after the current-stage logic, so it wins. An effect scrolls the map to that stage (animated, but not under Reduced Motion). A 'held' ref keeps the map on the chosen stage when levels.db is read again a moment later and moves the current stage on. Any tap on a node or gate, a drag, or a chapter jump releases it.
Review issue 2: 'held' is now also released when the map comes back with no stage chosen (select null), so the current stage leads the scroll again.
The loop-15 recreate restore (flowStack restoredHomeState, levels/shownResult.ts, the 'select' param) is unchanged. There are no new strings.

- levelPlayBack.test.tsx 'the result's למפה chooses' (real LevelPlayFlow and real levels store): a first play with the next three stages already played dismisses to select n+4 (the new current stage); a replay dismisses to select n+1.

New part (review issue 3, the exact QA path): play L002-L004 through 'לשלב הבא' as first plays, 'למפה' gives panel 5. Then tap node 1, 'שחק', 'לשלב הבא' twice (L002, then L003, all replays), 'למפה'. The same mounted map shows panel 'שלב 4' and scrolls to openOffset(4), and the URL is /levels?select=L004&pick=….

rework.notes:
The review's three issues are resolved.

items.rootCause: The result's 'למפה' (and Android back on the result) called router.dismissTo('/levels') with no params. The map stays mounted under the stage route, so it kept its own React state: the stage picked earlier (L001 or L008) and the scroll position. LevelMapScreen moved the choice and the scroll only when currentLevel changed (seenCurrent and follow(current)). Replaying an older stage never changes the current stage, so the map came back on the old pick. The 'select' param was also read only in the first useState, so even the quick-entry-off 'לשלב הבא', which already passed select, could not move a map that was already mounted.
items.fix:
apps/mobile/app/levels/play.tsx: the result's 'למפה' and back on the result go through resultToMap. It calls dismissTo({pathname:'/levels', params:{select, pick}}). pick = routeKey:run.n changes on every run, so the same stage can be chosen twice in a row. select comes from a new pure function, mapAfterAttempt (in mapModel.ts):
(a) A stage played for the first time that moved the current stage on: select is the new current stage. This keeps the case QA already passed (review issue 1): L018 played with L019-L033 played before goes to L034, 'השלב הבא'. In plain play, N goes to N+1.
(b) A stage played before (a replay): select is the stage after it, the one 'לשלב הבא' starts (L007 to L008, L010 to L011).
(c) No next stage open (a gate still shut, or L300): select is the played stage.
'First play' is read once when the run starts, from levels.db's records before the attempt (plays === 0). For a result restored after a recreate, the records already include the attempt, so the check there is plays <= 1. If levels.db is not read yet or there is no account, it counts as false and rule (b) applies.
A leave with no result (onLeave, back on 'מוכן?') still goes to the plain map. The quick-entry-off 'לשלב הבא' uses the same toMapAt. apps/mobile/app/levels/index.tsx passes 'pick' on.
LevelMapScreen.tsx: a select/pick pair (chosenTag) sets the choice during render, after the current-stage logic, so it wins. An effect scrolls the map to that stage (animated, but not under Reduced Motion). A 'held' ref keeps the map on the chosen stage when levels.db is read again a moment later and moves the current stage on. Any tap on a node or gate, a drag, or a chapter jump releases it.
Review issue 2: 'held' is now also released when the map comes back with no stage chosen (select null), so the current stage leads the scroll again.
The loop-15 recreate restore (flowStack restoredHomeState, levels/shownResult.ts, the 'select' param) is unchanged. There are no new strings.

items.rootCause: app/_layout.tsx hid the system splash in an effect as soon as the fonts were ready. In an Android release build that is the first render, before the native side has drawn the app's own Splash. On top of that, Expo's default exit is a 400 ms accelerating fade, which stays almost opaque for most of its length. A signed-in player's profile comes from the phone cache within a few frames, so the auth gate dropped `splash` and SplashOverlay started its own 240 ms fade-out while the system splash was still fading over it. The only frames of the app's Splash anyone could see were its first entrance frame (spinner and tip; seats, wordmark and tagline still at opacity 0) faintly under the icon, and both splashes went together. Nothing tied the system splash's exit to the app's Splash having laid out, and nothing kept the app's Splash up while that exit ran.
items.fix:
New file apps/mobile/src/services/systemSplash.ts:
- holdSystemSplash() runs when the root layout is imported. It calls preventAutoHideAsync and setOptions({ duration: 200, fade: true }) for a short cross-fade (skipped in Expo Go).
- hideSystemSplashAfterLayout() runs hideAsync one requestAnimationFrame after the layout, once per run.
- hideSystemSplash() opens a 250 ms 'exiting' window (SYSTEM_SPLASH_HOLD_MS); useSystemSplashExiting() reads it.

Root layout:
- The hideAsync on fonts-ready is gone. SplashOverlay's first onLayout (new onFirstLayout prop) now triggers the hide. If no Splash is up at first layout, the content view's onLayout does it instead.
- The overlay is shown and the app is hidden from screen readers while `splash || systemSplashExiting`. So the app's Splash never fades out under the system splash; after that its 240 ms fade (200 ms with Reduced Motion) to Home or Login is unchanged.
- Safety nets: a 3 s timer after fonts-ready hides the system splash if no layout ever comes, and the ErrorBoundary hides it too.

No minimum time was added. A slow sign-in keeps the Splash up as before; a fast one waits at most the rest of the 250 ms window. logFirstScreen, useAfterFirstScreen, AmbientLayer, flowStack, +native-intent and the auth gate are not touched.

docs/design/motion.md §4.9 has a new 'splash.handoff' row covering normal and Reduced Motion.

items.deviceCheck:
Needs a new APK.

Phone signed in, Hebrew, Reduced Motion off:
1. Start a screen recording.
2. Force-stop the app (recents, swipe it away), then open it from the icon.
3. Stop the recording once Home shows and step through it frame by frame.

What must be seen, in this order:
(a) The system splash: the 5 ⚡ 9 icon on dark, about 1–2 s while the JS loads (this part is not changed).
(b) A short (~0.2 s) cross-fade from the icon into the app's dark Splash. The four shapes ● ▲ ■ ◆ pop in, 'SUDOKU FIGHT' with 'סודוקו פייט' under it, then 'לוח אחד. כולם פותרים. רק אחד מנצח.'. At the bottom: the spinner with 'טוען את הזירה…', then the 'טיפ' chip and a tip.
(c) The Splash then fades out (~0.24 s) to Home. The icon and the designed Splash must never disappear in the same frame, and the designed Splash must be fully visible (not faint under the icon) in at least one frame.

On a fast start (cached profile) the designed Splash is short, about 0.3–0.5 s in all, so use a screen recording rather than screenshots. To see it longer: turn on airplane mode before the force-stop, or test signed out, where it stays until the sign-in state is known and then fades to Login.

Repeat with Reduced Motion on in the app's Settings: the same order, with the Splash content appearing at once (no pops) and a 0.2 s fade to Home.

Also check that the app never stays stuck on the icon: at most ~3 s even if something goes wrong.

rep.notes:
- No strings were added, so no i18n run was needed.
- All five files are LF with no BOM (checked byte by byte). motion.md's diff against refs/qa/snap-loop17 is my one added row only. apps/mobile/src/components/ui/motion.ts was edited briefly to debug and is back to exactly as it was (no diff).
- Device limits:
  - The 'stays under the system splash' hold is a JS timer (250 ms), not a native callback; expo-splash-screen does not report when its exit animation ends. If the main thread stalls for a long time, both animations finish when it frees up, but the order still holds: the system splash is never hidden before the app's Splash has laid out.
  - The 1.5–2 s of system icon at start is the JS bundle load and is not changed. No minimum display time was added, since the spec does not ask for one; on a cached-profile start the designed Splash is visible for roughly 0.3–0.5 s.
  - The Brand entrance plays under the 200 ms system cross-fade.
- Test harness: renderRouter turns on Jest fake timers, and a requestAnimationFrame fired from timers advanced by waitFor ran outside act. So test 1 captures the frame callback and runs it inside act. Test 1 still prints harmless 'overlapping act() calls' console warnings (all assertions pass, and the suite passed on every run). The fast-sign-in test runs first in the file, so it does not inherit that act state.

issues.problem: On the scenario QA tested (signed in, cached profile, force-stop, cold start), the designed Splash's content still won't be seen. The new hold keeps the overlay only about 250 ms after hideAsync, and about 200 ms of that is under the system cross-fade. The Brand and tagline entrances take much longer than that, so the logo is half-drawn and the tagline is never fully visible. QA's checks ('מתחת ללוגו: לוח אחד. כולם פותרים...', the four shapes, the wordmark, then a fade to Home) will fail again.
issues.evidence:
parts.tsx: BRAND_ENTRANCE = { seatStagger: 80, wordmarkAt: 160, subAt: 280 }. Enter.tsx: riseMs 320, a fade is stateChange 240. SplashScreen.tsx: TAGLINE_AT = subAt + 120 = 400.

Times from the Splash's mount:
- the wordmark is fully in at 480 ms;
- 'סודוקו פייט' at 520 ms;
- the tagline starts at 400 ms and is full at 640 ms.

With a cached profile (useAuthGate: splash goes false a few frames after initAuth), covered = systemSplashExiting only. hideAsync runs about 1 rAF after onLayout and SYSTEM_SPLASH_HOLD_MS is 250, so the overlay starts its 240 ms fade at about 270 ms. The tagline therefore starts drawing while the overlay is already below about 45% opacity.

It is fully visible, without the icon over it, for only about 50 to 80 ms. The fixer's own device check gives only 'about 0.3–0.5 s in all' and accepts 'fully visible in at least one frame'.

The motion.md 'splash.handoff' row says 'the Splash's entrance (the four seats, the wordmark, the tagline) plays under that fade'. That is wrong: the fade is 200 ms and the entrance is 640 ms.
issues.suggestion:
When the Splash is the one the system splash uncovers, render Brand and the tagline without their entrance (entrance/enabled false during the handoff). The system cross-fade then is the entrance, and every element is in the first drawn frame.

The content still has to be on screen long enough to be seen. Take the 'short minimum' question to Moshe through the main session, since the spec has none and §22 asks for an open in under 2 s. For example: let the Splash leave no earlier than about 600–800 ms after the system splash is gone, or once its entrance has ended. Don't ship as fixed with about 50 ms of full visibility.

issues.problem: The order of the two splashes depends on a 250 ms JS wall-clock timer that starts when hideAsync is called. It is not tied to when the native exit animation actually runs. The QA evidence shows this phone's UI thread lagging about 1 s at startup. Under that stall both animations still end in the same frame, which is the original symptom. The fixer's notes admit this ('If the main thread stalls for a long time, both animations finish when it frees up').
issues.evidence:
Native side, node_modules/expo-splash-screen/android/.../SplashScreenManager.kt:
- An OnPreDrawListener on android.R.id.content returns false while keepSplashScreenOnScreen is true, so no app frame is drawn until hide().
- The exit animator (ViewPropertyAnimator on the UI thread, AccelerateInterpolator) starts only after the next draw.

So the first drawn frame after hide() already held the Splash in the old code too: the old fonts-ready effect ran in the same commit that mounted SplashOverlay. Moving hideAsync to after onLayout plus one rAF hardly changes anything natively. The only real change is the 250 ms hold.

The QA report on SM-A165F: the spinner and tip sat faintly under the icon for about 1 s with a 400 ms fade, and the Reanimated entrance (seats, wordmark) never moved. Both point to a UI thread that is blocked or late.

If the JS timer (250 ms) runs out while the UI thread is still busy with the Home mount under the Splash, the overlay's withTiming fade is queued. When the UI thread frees, both time-based animations jump to their end in one frame. With the accelerate curve the icon is still 44% opaque even 150 ms into its 200 ms fade, so 50 ms of slack is not enough.
issues.suggestion:
Pace the hold on the UI thread, not with setTimeout on the JS side. For example, use a Reanimated useFrameCallback (or UI-thread animation callbacks) that counts frames actually rendered after hide. Or wait for the Splash's own Enter completion callbacks, which only fire after UI frames have run. Only then let `covered` drop.

Prefer a rendered-frame count (for example 15 or more frames after the exit begins) over wall-clock time, so a stall can't collapse both exits into one frame. Then check it on phone 3 with a frame-by-frame screen recording.

issues.problem: In the 'Home first' path, hideAsync fires before any Splash is mounted. The cross-fade can show Home, then the Splash pops in over it for 250 ms, then fades back to Home (Home, Splash, Home). Test 2 locks this behaviour in.
issues.evidence:
When this path happens: useAppFonts uses expo-font's async useFonts, and useAuthGate/initAuth run before the `if (!fontsReady)` early return. A cached profile can therefore resolve before the fonts, so the first full render has splash false and covered false.

Then, in _layout.tsx, the content View's `onLayout={covered ? undefined : hideSystemSplashAfterLayout}` calls hideAsync. hideSystemSplash calls hideAsync and then setExiting(true). The Splash mounts (inMs 0) only on a later React render and Fabric commit, while hide() has already let the content view draw. So the first frames under the fading icon are Home.

systemSplashHandoff.e2e.test.tsx test 2 asserts that 'the Splash comes back over Home'.
issues.suggestion: In that path, call setExiting(true) first so the Splash mounts. Then hide the system splash only from SplashOverlay's onFirstLayout, never from the content View's onLayout. Change test 2 to assert that hideAsync is called only after the overlay's layout, even when the sign-in was known first.

issues.problem: The ambient layer and the first-screen work don't follow the new 'covered' state.
issues.evidence: _layout.tsx: `<AmbientLayer covered={splash} />`, `useAfterFirstScreen(fontsReady && !splash, …)` and `logFirstScreen` all still use `splash`, not `covered`. During the hold window the Splash is still on screen, but the ambient drift clock runs under it. motion.md (line 41 and the ambient.drift row) says that clock stops while the Splash covers the app. logFirstScreen also records the first screen up to 250 ms before it is actually visible.
issues.suggestion: Pass `covered` to AmbientLayer, and decide whether logFirstScreen/useAfterFirstScreen should wait for `!covered`. That keeps the docs and the startup metrics honest.

issues.problem: The tests check only the JS call order, not the order the user sees on the phone. Test 1 also needs a hand-run rAF inside act and prints 'overlapping act() calls' warnings.
issues.evidence:
What I ran: jest systemSplashHandoff and startupGraph (36/36 pass). Related suites (screens/account, ambient*, accounts, latestRoot, roomLinks, rankedResume, screens/home): 45 suites, 718 tests, all pass. tsc -p apps/mobile is clean, and eslint on the 4 changed code files is clean.

On Android, though, what appears on screen depends on the native OnPreDrawListener and the UI-thread animators. None of that is modelled, so the passing tests do not show that the reported symptom is fixed.

items.rootCause:
Four things together:
1. app/_layout.tsx hid the system splash in an effect as soon as the fonts were ready, with Expo's default 400 ms accelerating fade. Nothing tied that hide to the app's Splash having been drawn.
2. When the sign-in was known before the fonts (a cached profile), the first full render had no Splash at all. The system splash then uncovered Home, or the Splash appeared over Home.
3. The Splash under the icon played its own entrance: seats 0–320 ms, wordmark at 160–480 ms, tagline at 400–640 ms. The icon and the Splash's 240 ms fade-out were both over long before that, so only the spinner and tip were ever drawn (faint, under the icon). This is exactly what QA saw.
4. Nothing kept the Splash up after the system splash's exit. My first fix used a 250 ms JS setTimeout for that, which a stalled UI thread (phone 3 lags about 1 s at start) collapses into one frame together with the native exit animator.
items.fix:
services/systemSplash.ts is now a 4-phase store: off, held, exiting, done.
- held: set at the root layout's import (dev and release builds). preventAutoHideAsync plus setOptions({ duration: 200, fade: true }).
- The Splash covers the app from the first full render while the phase is held or exiting (`covered = splash || useSystemSplashCovering()`), whatever the sign-in already knows. So the system splash always uncovers the Splash, never Home. The content View's onLayout hide is gone.
- The system splash is hidden only from SplashOverlay's first onLayout, one requestAnimationFrame later (phase exiting).
- The Splash mounted under the system splash has no entrance (Brand entrance and the tagline's Enter are off, decided on mount). Every element (four seats, wordmark, name, tagline, spinner, tip) is in its first frame, and the 200 ms cross-fade is its entrance. A Splash that mounts later in a run keeps its entrance.
- The hold is counted on the UI thread, not on a JS timer. While exiting, SplashOverlay mounts a SystemSplashPacer (Reanimated useFrameCallback, registered only then). It counts frames from its first frame. A frame counts as 'seen' only once 200 + 50 ms (exit + margin) have passed. done = SPLASH_SEEN_FRAMES (9 at 60 Hz) seen frames AND at least 250 + splashSeenMs ms. After a stall, the first late frame counts as one frame only, so the Splash still stays alone for 8 more drawn frames. Then the phase is done, and the Splash fades out (240 ms; Reduced Motion 200) to Home or Login once the sign-in is known.
- New setting accountConfig.splashSeenMs = 150: the Splash's time alone and whole. The spec has no minimum and §22 wants the first screen in under 2 s, so it is short and documented as Moshe's to raise. In total, a fast start reaches Home about 0.24 s later than before.
- Fail-safes: the system splash goes 3 s after fonts-ready at the latest; exiting ends 3 s after it started at the latest; the ErrorBoundary hides without a handoff.
- Expo Go, and Jest by default, has no handoff (phase off) and hides at fonts-ready as before, so other suites are unchanged.
- From review: AmbientLayer, useAfterFirstScreen and logFirstScreen now follow `covered`, so the ambient clock stops under the Splash and the metric is when Home is actually shown.
- motion.md 'splash.handoff' row rewritten.
- flowStack, +native-intent, the auth gate and startupGraph are untouched.

apps/mobile/src/__tests__/systemSplashHandoff.e2e.test.tsx, 6 tests. The e2e tests render the real root layout through renderRouter with a development build (isRunningInExpoGo false) and expo-splash-screen mocked.
1. At import: held, with setOptions({ duration: 200, fade: true }).
2. Slow sign-in: hideAsync is not called at ready, and is called once a frame after the overlay's layout. The Splash stays after the handoff until the sign-in arrives, then goes to Home.
3. Sign-in known at once, full motion:

rework.notes:
How each review point was handled:
- High 1 (content never seen): fixed. There is no entrance under the system splash, so every element is in the first drawn frame. On top of that, the Splash stays alone and whole for accountConfig.splashSeenMs (150 ms, and at least 9 drawn frames).
- Open decision for Moshe: the spec has no minimum, and §22 wants the first screen in under 2 s. That is why the value is a setting and short; Moshe can raise it (e.g. 600) for a Splash that people can read. Please pass this to the main session.
- High 2 (wall-clock hold): fixed. The hold is counted in UI-thread frames, and after a stall the first late frame counts once.
- Medium (Home first): fixed. The Splash covers from the first render while the system splash is held, and the hide comes only from the overlay's layout. The test that locked in the Home → Splash → Home order was replaced.
- Lows: AmbientLayer, logFirstScreen and useAfterFirstScreen now follow `covered`. Device verification is still required (see deviceCheck); the tests check only the JS order.

Other notes:
- No strings were added, so no i18n run was needed.
- All 7 changed files are LF with no BOM (checked byte-wise).
- motion.md, account.ts and ambientEverywhere.test.ts differ from refs/qa/snap-loop17 only by my lines.
- components/ui/motion.ts was edited briefly to debug and is back to its exact prior content.

Test-harness findings, for anyone else writing these tests:
- RNTL's fireEvent(…, 'layout') on a Reanimated Animated.View left that overlay's later state updates unapplied (usePresence's setMounted after the fade). The test calls the overlay's onLayout prop directly instead.
- Reanimated's frame-callback loop is one per module. A full-motion test that leaves an ambient frame callback running ties that loop to its own fake clock, so the slow-sign-in test runs first and with Reduced Motion.
- ranked.e2e failed once ('Cannot set properties of undefined (setting startTime)', in Reanimated's frame registry). That run had the pacer's frame callback registered for the whole run. It now mounts only during the exit, and ranked.e2e passed on both later runs.

items.rootCause:
Four things together:
1. app/_layout.tsx hid the system splash in an effect as soon as the fonts were ready, with Expo's default 400 ms accelerating fade. Nothing tied that hide to the app's Splash having been drawn.
2. When the sign-in was known before the fonts (a cached profile), the first full render had no Splash at all. The system splash then uncovered Home, or the Splash appeared over Home.
3. The Splash under the icon played its own entrance: seats 0–320 ms, wordmark at 160–480 ms, tagline at 400–640 ms. The icon and the Splash's 240 ms fade-out were both over long before that, so only the spinner and tip were ever drawn (faint, under the icon). This is exactly what QA saw.
4. Nothing kept the Splash up after the system splash's exit. My first fix used a 250 ms JS setTimeout for that, which a stalled UI thread (phone 3 lags about 1 s at start) collapses into one frame together with the native exit animator.
items.fix:
services/systemSplash.ts is now a 4-phase store: off, held, exiting, done.
- held: set at the root layout's import (dev and release builds). preventAutoHideAsync plus setOptions({ duration: 200, fade: true }).
- The Splash covers the app from the first full render while the phase is held or exiting (`covered = splash || useSystemSplashCovering()`), whatever the sign-in already knows. So the system splash always uncovers the Splash, never Home. The content View's onLayout hide is gone.
- The system splash is hidden only from SplashOverlay's first onLayout, one requestAnimationFrame later (phase exiting).
- The Splash mounted under the system splash has no entrance (Brand entrance and the tagline's Enter are off, decided on mount). Every element (four seats, wordmark, name, tagline, spinner, tip) is in its first frame, and the 200 ms cross-fade is its entrance. A Splash that mounts later in a run keeps its entrance.
- The hold is counted on the UI thread, not on a JS timer. While exiting, SplashOverlay mounts a SystemSplashPacer (Reanimated useFrameCallback, registered only then). It counts frames from its first frame. A frame counts as 'seen' only once 200 + 50 ms (exit + margin) have passed. done = SPLASH_SEEN_FRAMES (9 at 60 Hz) seen frames AND at least 250 + splashSeenMs ms. After a stall, the first late frame counts as one frame only, so the Splash still stays alone for 8 more drawn frames. Then the phase is done, and the Splash fades out (240 ms; Reduced Motion 200) to Home or Login once the sign-in is known.
- New setting accountConfig.splashSeenMs = 150: the Splash's time alone and whole. The spec has no minimum and §22 wants the first screen in under 2 s, so it is short and documented as Moshe's to raise. In total, a fast start reaches Home about 0.24 s later than before.
- Fail-safes: the system splash goes 3 s after fonts-ready at the latest; exiting ends 3 s after it started at the latest; the ErrorBoundary hides without a handoff.
- Expo Go, and Jest by default, has no handoff (phase off) and hides at fonts-ready as before, so other suites are unchanged.
- From review: AmbientLayer, useAfterFirstScreen and logFirstScreen now follow `covered`, so the ambient clock stops under the Splash and the metric is when Home is actually shown.
- motion.md 'splash.handoff' row rewritten.
- flowStack, +native-intent, the auth gate and startupGraph are untouched.
items.test:
apps/mobile/src/__tests__/systemSplashHandoff.e2e.test.tsx, 6 tests. The e2e tests render the real root layout through renderRouter with a development build (isRunningInExpoGo false) and expo-splash-screen mocked.
1. At import: held, with setOptions({ duration: 200, fade: true }).
2. Slow sign-in: hideAsync is not called at ready, and is called once a frame after the overlay's layout. The Splash stays after the handoff until the sign-in arrives, then goes to Home.
3. Sign-in known at once, full motion:
   - auth is 'ready' but the overlay covers, Home is hidden and hideAsync is not called (old code: Home first, or hidden at ready);
   - seats 0 and 3, the wordmark and the tagline are not at opacity 0 (old code: the entrance starts at 0);
   - hideAsync runs a frame after the layout, and a second layout does nothing;
   - the phase ends by the frame pacer at no less than 400 ms and under the fail-safe, and only then does Home show and the Splash unmount.
4. Unit, holdStep: frames during the exit don't count. A 2 s stall gives 1 seen frame and not done; done comes only after SPLASH_SEEN_FRAMES. On a 120 Hz display, enough frames but too little time is not done.
5. Unit: hidden once, a frame after the layout. Still covering long past the old 250 ms wall-clock hold until the frames say so (old code fails here), with the 3 s fail-safe as backup.
6. Unit: the fail-safe and Expo Go (off) paths.

Checked against old behaviour:
- Forcing the Brand entrance back on fails test 3.
- Putting back the fonts-ready hide fails tests 2 and 3.

Also updated: ambientEverywhere.test.ts (source check, now `<AmbientLayer covered={covered} />` and `const covered = splash || systemSplashCovering`).

Run: all of apps/mobile/src/__tests__ (every e2e, startupGraph, reducedMotion, the docs tests), plus screens/account, screens/home, components/ambient, config and theme. 119 suites, 2133 tests, all pass, with no act warnings in the new file. tsc -p apps/mobile, eslint and prettier on the changed files are clean.
items.deviceCheck:
Needs a new APK. Phone 3 (SM-A165F), signed in, Hebrew, Reduced Motion off.
1. Start a screen recording.
2. Force-stop the app (recents, swipe away), then open it from the icon.
3. Stop the recording once Home shows, and step through it frame by frame.

What must be seen, in this order:
(a) The system icon (5 ⚡ 9 on dark) while the JS loads, about 1–2 s (this part is not changed).
(b) A short (~0.2 s) cross-fade from the icon into the app's dark Splash. Already in the first frame of the cross-fade, and not popping in afterwards:
   - all four shapes ● ▲ ■ ◆ in four colours;
   - 'SUDOKU FIGHT' with 'סודוקו פייט' under it;
   - 'לוח אחד. כולם פותרים. רק אחד מנצח.';
   - at the bottom, the spinner with 'טוען את הזירה…', then the 'טיפ' chip and a tip.
(c) After the icon is completely gone, the Splash alone and fully opaque for at least ~0.2 s (about 6 or more frames in a 30 fps recording). The icon and the Splash must never disappear in the same frame.
(d) The Splash fades out (~0.24 s) to Home.

Repeat with Reduced Motion on in the app's Settings: the same order, and a 0.2 s fade to Home.

Repeat signed out (or in airplane mode): the same handoff, then the Splash stays until the sign-in state is known, then goes to Login or Home.

The app must never stay on the icon for more than ~3 s after the JS has loaded.
